key: Save him who bringeth unto Allah a whole heart.
s: Abraham’s prayer turns to the day of raising, when wealth and sons avail nothing, and names the one exception; al-Tabari, on 26:85 to 26:89, reads the ‘whole heart’ as one free of doubt about God’s oneness and the raising after death.

opened.locator: comment on 26:85 to 26:89 (one segment), at the words illa man ata Allaha bi-qalbin salim

evidence.words: والذي عني به من سلامة القلب في هذا الموضع: هو سلامة القلب من الشكّ في توحيد الله، والبعث بعد الممات.
evidence.gloss: What is meant by soundness of heart in this place is the heart’s soundness from doubt about the oneness of God and about the raising after death.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Ash-Shu’ara 26:89, at 3020); it is its own sentence in day.js. al-Tabari comments on 26:85 to 26:89 as one segment and, in his own voice, says the sound heart here is one sound from doubt about God’s oneness and the resurrection after death, then cites Muhammad (Ibn Sirin), Mujahid, Qatada, Ibn Zayd and al-Dahhak in support. The sentence paraphrases his statement without adding the reporters’ variants. Plain sense faithful: Abraham’s prayer (26:83 to 26:89) reaches the day of raising when wealth and sons avail not (26:87 to 26:88). Two words of the key verse quoted. Entry-check ok, no changes.
